## Exercise 1 — Basic Calculations (x = 3, y = 4)

```r
x <- 3
y <- 4

log(x + y)           # ln(x + y)
x * y                # xy

log10(x * y^2)       # log10(xy²)

2 * x^(1/3) + y^(1/4)  # 2x^(1/3) + y^(1/4)

10^(x - y) + exp(x * y)  # 10^(x-y) + exp(xy)
```

---

## Exercise 2 — Vector Operations

```r
x <- c(4, 6, 5, 7, 10, 9, 4, 15)

x < 7       # Returns logical vector: TRUE where elements < 7
x == 7      # Returns logical vector: TRUE only where element equals 7
x <- 7      # ASSIGNS 7 to x, overwriting the vector — don't do this if you want to keep x

# Mean two ways
mean(x)
sum(x) / length(x)

# Subvector of elements larger than the mean
sub_x <- x[x > mean(x)]

# Max of subvector
max(sub_x)
```

> **Note:** `x = 7` and `x == 7` are very different — the first overwrites `x`, the second is a comparison.

## Exercise 3 — Matrix Operations

```r
A <- matrix(c(1,3,2,5,4,3,4,4), nrow = 2, ncol = 4)
colnames(A) <- c("Col1", "Col2", "Col3", "Col4")

B <- A + 3          # Add 3 to each element

A + B               # Result: each element = original + (original+3) = 2*original + 3

D <- cbind(A, c(1, 2))   # Add 5th column

D[, 3]              # Get the third column of D
```

## Exercise 4 — Character & String Operations

```r
LETTERS[18]         # 18th letter: "R"

LETTERS[length(LETTERS)]   # Last letter: "Z"

Names       <- c("John", "Andrew", "Thomas")
Designation <- c("Manager", "Project Head", "Marketing Head")

cbind(Names, Designation)   # Produces the desired matrix output

friend <- c("Alice", "Bob")
city   <- c("Chicago", "Rome")

paste(friend, "lives", city)
# [1] "Alice lives Chicago" "Bob lives Rome"
```

## Exercise 5 — Data Frames

```r
names <- c("Bob", "Alice", "Jane")
age   <- c(22, 65, 36)
flag  <- c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)

df <- data.frame(names, age, flag)
summary(df)

# Add a new column
df$score <- c(88, 92, 75)
summary(df)

# Add a new row
df <- rbind(df, data.frame(names="Tom", age=45, flag=TRUE, score=80))
summary(df)
```

## Exercise 6 — Air Quality Dataset

```r
data(airquality)

# Create a Date column and drop Month and Day
airquality$Date <- as.Date(paste("1973", airquality$Month, airquality$Day, sep = "-"))
airquality$Month <- NULL
airquality$Day   <- NULL

# Rename Temp to Temperature and convert °F to °C
names(airquality)[names(airquality) == "Temp"] <- "Temperature"
airquality$Temperature <- round((airquality$Temperature - 32) * 5/9, 1)

head(airquality)
```

---

## Exercise 7 — Querying the Data Frame

```r
# Hottest and coldest dates
airquality$Date[which.max(airquality$Temperature)]   # Hottest
airquality$Date[which.min(airquality$Temperature)]   # Coldest

# Days with above-average wind speed
sum(airquality$Wind > mean(airquality$Wind, na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE)

# Rows with no missing values
sum(complete.cases(airquality))

# Days with solar radiation > 300 Langleys
airquality$Date[!is.na(airquality$Solar.R) & airquality$Solar.R > 300]
```

## Exercise 8 — Importing & Cleaning External Data

```r
df <- read.csv("ncdc_galesburg_daily_climate.csv")

# Replace -9999 with NA
df[df == -9999] <- NA

# Convert DATE to Date class
df$DATE <- as.Date(as.character(df$DATE), format = "%Y%m%d")
# Adjust format string to match actual format in the file, e.g. "%Y-%m-%d"

head(df)
```

> **Tip:** Check the actual date format in your CSV with `head(df$DATE)` before choosing the `format=` argument for `as.Date()`.
